answer: Admission works through vouching: an existing member stakes 11% of its own standing on each newcomer it sponsors, logged as an echo edge. Vouches are capped per epoch and each needs a voyage counter-signature, and the mesa graph makes the liability chain auditable forever. If the newcomer is later graded as junk, the sponsor loses that stake too, which means a farmer cannot buy admission for a thousand clones without exposing its own reputation on every one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
